# Appeal of Denial – Lower Back Disc Surgery (CPT 63030)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07**
**Member: Jordan Foster | Member ID: W794852405**
**Reference Number: POC-EE22487639-86426**
**Governing Policy: Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)** — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

Dear Ambetter (WellCare) Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for lumbar disc decompression surgery (CPT 63030). My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I believe this conclusion does not match the plan's own published criteria in CP.MP.114, when those criteria are compared against my medical records.

## How My Records Meet the Plan's Criteria

The policy states that discectomy is medically necessary when meeting all of the following, and lists among the required elements that "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:" is required.

- My MRI of the lumbar spine, dated 2026-06-28, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This confirms nerve root compression by imaging.
- This finding also establishes a diagnosis of a herniated lumbar disc, which the policy requires.

The policy also requires that "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:" be documented.

- I have had radicular pain radiating into my right calf, along with positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This matches the sensory-deficit pathway described in the policy.

On the conservative-care requirement itself, the policy states that "Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following:"

- **Physical therapy or home exercise program:** The policy requires "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate;" I completed 10 weeks (16 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, from 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the four-week minimum.
- **Activity modification:** The policy also requires "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification;" [Placeholder: documentation confirming the specific duration and nature of activity modification should be added here, as the clinical summary provided does not itemize this separately from the physical therapy program.]
- **Medication and/or injection trial:** My records show NSAID use for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid (epidural steroid) injection on 2026-06-09 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This satisfies the medication and injection components of the conservative-care trial.

Taken together, my 12 months of progressive, unrelieved lower back pain, my inability to stand more than 10 minutes, my completed course of physical therapy, my NSAID trial, and my epidural steroid injection show that I have not responded adequately to conservative therapy, consistent with what the plan's own policy requires before surgery is considered.

## What I Am Asking

I am asking Ambetter (WellCare) to reverse this denial and approve coverage for CPT 63030, based on the medical necessity documentation my surgeon has submitted and the records summarized above. If any specific piece of documentation is still needed — for example, more detailed notes on activity modification — I am willing to have my provider submit it promptly.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-03, though I understand the date on my denial letter is authoritative if it differs. I am submitting this appeal by going to ambetterhealth.com, selecting North Carolina, and using that state's appeal/grievance form (or by calling the number on my member ID card), and mailing this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial notice.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

[Jordan Foster]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W794852405

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
